header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tmp1364.tmp1364.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.urn:cts:latinLit:tmp1364.tmp1364.opp-lat: Several passages are syntactically broken (anacolutha typical of the document), notably the Umbriacum sentence in line 4 and the opening of the basilica bequest in line 5; bracketed words supply the sense. 'quae memorare novero' is emended in the edition to 'non valeo'; translated accordingly. 'Tricurino', 'Vicinoniae', 'Nimione', 'Frontanito', 'Thedone', 'Buresaco' are not securely identified. *palastriae* is obscure (perhaps vine-props or plots). 'Majorem domnus' read as 'maiorem domus'. 'ad matrico' read as 'ad matriculam' (poor-roll). 'pro collata principis caelestis' is corrupt; sense conjectured. 'inditas' read as 'inclitus'; 'taro' as 'tam'; 'cura' as 'cum'.

Line 6: 'vitias' read as 'villas'. 'Colonica' in the list may be a place name or the term *colonica*; taken as a name. 'pro tutelam percepi' (Portithorengum) is obscure, rendered 'received in guardianship'. 'hunc ego absens vi' is garbled; sense approximate. The passage on Chlothar's 'despoiling' is syntactically loose. Line 7: 'pictas' read as 'pietas'; 'durissime' as 'dulcissime'. Line 8: 'si supersistit ut' and 'si semper corpus' are unclear; rendered by sense. Line 9: 'domui Petri' read as 'domni Petri'; 'cura vineis' as 'cum vineis'; 'filio Papoleno' may mean 'from Papolenus's son' or 'from my son Papolenus'.

Text is formulaic and in places ungrammatical; renderings follow the evident sense. 'pro bis' (11) read as 'pro his'; 'obsistente' taken as 'despite opposition'. 'Perfeci' (11) may be corrupt. In 12, 'propterca' read as 'propterea'; the syntax around 'Ecclesia stipendia et madricola' is broken. 'necutiante' (14) read as 'negotiante' (merchant). In 14 'stabilius' probably for 'stabilivi' or 'stat'; the closing address 'sancta Ecclesia, domni Petri et Pauli' seems to mean the basilica. 'cet' (13) read as 'et'. Pontochiuggane and Saboranense unidentified.

Line 15: 'miracula' is evidently a corruption, probably for a word meaning dependency (e.g. 'matricula'/'mancipiola'); rendered by sense. 'tribulum Taletense' read as 'tributum'. Line 17: 'precarias' (variant 'picarias') uncertain: either holders by precarial tenure or pitch-workers; 'pixita' taken as pitch-works, given 'pix'. 'cimencitia' taken as 'caementicia' (stone-built). Line 18: 'mensae' taken as altars; 'e contra pontifice' obscure, rendered tentatively.

Line 19: *damea* (variant *clavia*) is obscure, a type of garment or fabric. 'cabellum' taken as caballum (horse); 'pareculum' unclear, perhaps a small pair (of vessels or garments). 'ex militia' rendered 'from my service'. Line 20: 'Warannonis' taken as stallions (warannio); 'spadas' geldings. The last sentence ('Jumenta dei illo...') is garbled; 'dei illo' perhaps for 'de illo'. Line 21: 'Diablentas' identified as Jublains; 'bessorum' and the name 'Blado Victribernus' are uncertain. The Berulfus clause is broken. Line 22: 'obedum civitatis' doubtful, the edition suggests 'ob tus in civitate'. The Redonatiacum sentence lacks a main verb. Line 23: 'horae recordationis' read as 'bonae recordationis'; 'Majores domos' as mayor of the palace; 'precaluriam' as *precaria*. Line 24: the Vocriomnum sentence is syntactically broken.

25: 'De Marogilo villas Rufiniaco et Marigilo' is awkward and probably corrupt; rendered literally. 26: the first sentence (Suadria's gift) has no main verb and seems incomplete. 27: 'habere nolo' ('I do not wish to have') contradicts the context; read as 'volo' ('I wish'). 'ia civem' is read with the edition's note as 'in civitatem'. 'Gutia' is taken as Gothia (Septimania/Aquitaine). 29: 'caballis padi [F., paria] duo, et poledros congregans duos, et singulos parioculos' is obscure and probably corrupt; the rendering 'two pairs of horses… two colts… each a pair' is tentative. Chaimoaldus is spelled here 'Cabimoaldus' (a scanning variant), with the edition's note identifying him as bishop of Poitiers.

Line 30: 'Emmane cum uxore' is odd if Emma is female; may be a male name. 'Dasgastaldus' appears corrupt (perhaps for 'de gasindis' or similar); rendered by sense as 'those of them'. 'in Albis' taken as the white-garment festival (Easter/Whitsun). Line 32: the sum for Saint Richomer is missing in the text. Line 34: 'sicut domni et antecessores nostri fecerunt' reads as if a negative is understood; '[not]' supplied tentatively. Line 35: 'aedificavit' has no expressed subject; 'Casellas illas quas bonae memoriae. Domnigisilus' has a misplaced full stop, ignored.

'tentaverim' is first person in the text ('if I should attempt'), evidently for 'tentaverit'; translated as third person to agree with 'si quis'. 'nemine' read as 'nomine'. 'Honoratus' after Guntinus and Hugo may be a title (a local notable, *honoratus*) or a second name. Only six witnesses besides the notary appear, though seven are announced; the list may be incomplete.

nodes.text: THE WILL OF SAINT BERTRAM, BISHOP OF LE MANS.
(Mabillon, Analecta, vol. I, p. 255.)

There follows a copy of the will of the aforesaid lord Bertram, which he made jointly for the mother church of Le Mans and for the monastery of Saint Peter, as it is inserted here. We insert it into these deeds of the bishops for this reason: that if, God forbid, it should be lost through any negligence, it may be found here, so that it may be known how it was done.

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ and of the Holy Spirit, on the sixth day before the Kalends of April, in the 32nd year of the reign of the most glorious lord King Chlothar, I, Bertram, although unworthy, a sinner, bishop of the holy Church of Le Mans, sound, by God's favour, in mind and body, and with sound judgement, fearing the chances of human frailty, have made my will, and asked my son Ebbo the notary to write it, and dictated it. And if by any chance this my will cannot be valid under civil law or praetorian law, or through the intervention of any new law, I wish it to be valid as if [made] by one intestate, in the place of codicils, and let it be valid. Therefore, when I, the above-written Bertram, a sinner, shall have departed from human affairs, or completed the time owed to nature, then you, most holy Church of Le Mans, together with the holy and venerable basilica of the lords Peter and Paul the apostles, which I built by my own work in sight of the city for the defence of the city and the health of the people, be my heirs; and I establish and order that you are my heirs, and let all others be wholly disinherited. Whatever, then, I shall have given, bequeathed, or ordered to be given by this my will, I commit to the good faith of my heirs that it be given, done, and rendered; and any whom I shall have ordered to be free, let them all, women and men, be free. And since the renowned and most excellent lord King Chlothar, to whom may God repay eternal blessedness a thousandfold, gave me his precept confirmed in law by his own hand, granting me free choice to assign from my own property, what I have from the inheritance of my parents, or what I obtained by his gift, or bought anything, or may be able to buy with God's help, or may be able to increase in any goods and holdings of property, as well for the remedy of my soul as to my relatives or to my faithful men, as I wish; therefore I wish and order that you, most holy Church of Le Mans, my heir, have the estate of my right called Bonalfa, situated in the territory of Étampes or the Yveline forest, which the most excellent lord King Chlothar by his gift, together with the most excellent lady Queen Fredegund, his late mother, granted to me, their humble [servant], after lord Vaedola had rendered justice to them, for the keeping of my faith, which I have always been seen to hold and maintain inviolate towards that prince; that estate, with houses, slaves, vineyards, woods, fields, and every thing, right and appurtenance, movable as well as immovable, you may possess in perpetuity after my death, excepting those whom I shall wish to free from there. Likewise I wish and decree that you, lady Church my heir, have the field acquired for cultivation at that time; half of which field the lady Ingoberga of good memory, the late queen, left to Saint Mary at my urging and in return for my service; the other half I bought for a price paid from her brother, the late Magnulf, so that that field might come wholly into the right of the holy church; and concerning the estate of Celonica, situated in the territory of Tricurinum, half of which Bobelenus of good memory had assigned to the Church, and on account of that half I suffered many vexations, but by my efforts I brought it about that it was not taken from the right of the holy Church; and afterwards I also bought outright for a price paid the other half, which he had assigned to his wife and heirs to possess, and it came into my ownership; I wish that you, most holy Church my heir, [have] that estate with all security, together with the shrine of Vicinonia, whatever I bought for myself or settled with slaves by my efforts, with whatever I may still, God willing, be able to improve in those fields, with all their entirety, and the slaves dwelling there; I wish it to be given to you, most holy Church. Likewise the estate of Brea, which Daulfus conferred on me by deed of gift, and which I afterwards bought, along with whatever I added to it: let that estate, with all its entirety, as it is possessed by me at the present time, remain in the ownership of the holy Church of Le Mans, my heir. But also very many things, which I know [I cannot] recount, I acquired for you, holy Church, by my effort.

And although it is known to all, by Christ's favour, how and how faithfully I laboured in the holy Church, or in the monasteries, or in all affairs, yet you also, lord bishop, whom God shall wish to be over them after me, can learn how much God deigned to confer there by my effort and labour in my time. If you are minded to inquire with complete good faith, you will find that I have laboured not a little for your Church. Hence it ought not to seem unfitting to you if I leave anything from the property of Saint Mary in usufruct to any of our brothers, that is priests and deacons, or readers, or to my relatives, or friends, or servants, as well of the holy Church as my own, to whomever; for I do not take away the holy Church's ownership, and I make it heir of my little substance. And since lord Domnolus of holy memory, the late bishop, assigned some small places from the Church's lands to his basilica, where he lies at rest, it was distasteful to us that we in turn, on a similar footing, should take away or diminish anything from the Church's lands in order to confer it on the basilica of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, which I built in honour of their name; but rather, deliberating with the counsel of our venerable brothers the priests and deacons and all the clergy, [it was resolved] that one small place of the Church's tenure [should go] to that holy basilica, not so much from necessity as for the first-fruits and reverence of the lord apostles themselves, and because the holy mother Church, which cherishes and enriches all the basilicas belonging to her, agreed with the lord bishops on that day on which the heavenly blessing and the relics of the holy apostles Peter and Paul were placed in that basilica, and it was doubly consecrated by divine grace by holy bishops in honour of the holy apostles, and on the consecration of that place: [namely] the estate of Umbriacum, which Basilius and Baudegundus, now dead, had made over by deed of gift to the holy Church, to be possessed after their death; for which we afterwards laboured continually so that it should not be taken from the Church; thereafter all the aforesaid that has accrued or come to the holy Church through my humble self, both the aforesaid Umbriacum and in the suburban basilica of the lords Peter and Paul the apostles, which is known to have been built by my work, ought, by Christ's favour, to remain in perpetuity to that holy Church.

It has pleased me to assign this: that the estate of Nimio, situated in the territory of Paris, with the vineyards at Frontanitum which are known to be for the *palastriae* and vinedressers, which lord King Chlothar gave me, which I [held] often while I was a layman, both from the fisc and by purchase, I wish to be given wholly to be possessed by the holy Church of Paris, under whose grace I was brought up. To the basilica of the holy and most blessed apostles Peter and Paul, which I established above as heir together with the holy Church of Le Mans, as is my devotion, since I desire to lay my poor body there (whenever God wills), to that holy basilica in honour of the holy apostles, so that, for the crime which I have been seen continually to commit here in the world, the apostles themselves may deign by their intercession to free me from infernal punishment, and if not into glory (which I do not merit), I may at least deserve to obtain pardon through their patronage or intercession: I therefore give to that holy basilica the estates situated in the territory of Le Mans as well as in that of Étampes or of Bordeaux, or wherever, both those I already gave to that basilica by deed of gift on its dedication day, and also what I shall still give by the page of this will, which the glorious lord Chlothar conferred on me by his munificence, or for the keeping of my faith, by his precepts confirmed by his hand, granted me full licence to confer on the aforesaid place, for the remedy of my soul and the stability of his kingdom, those estates which I earned by his gift. These are the estates: the estate of Thedo; a *colonica* named Telate; and other estates at Buresacum; and the dwellings in the Gâtinais, which we received from the illustrious man Warnachar, mayor of the palace, in exchange for the estate of Columbaria. This I ask and order of the abbots who in each age, as divine power or the grace of the lord apostles shall command them to continue there, that throughout their life this be most especially observed by them: that of whatever may come in each year from the estates named above, whether in tribute or in aid, half be distributed to the poor, in clothing or in money, when my commemoration takes place; with the other half let lights be kindled sufficiently in the holy basilica at all times, so that the holy basilica is never without lights for a single hour of the night; it is a fitting sign that in honour of the aforesaid apostles light should shine unceasingly at all times, both at the basilica of the holy apostles, and at the Holy Cross, which I built afterwards, and at the basilica of lord Martin at the hospice which is in Pontlieue; excepting the fruits and other dues expected from the aforesaid lands for the uses of the holy basilica and its monastery, or the sustenance of the canons or of the poor who sit on the register at that holy basilica: let food and clothing be supplied sufficiently every year, and let them pray to the Lord continually for the expiation of my sins, and for the prince, in return for what he conferred, that the heavenly [King] may grant him a long reign, and that he may deserve to receive a hundredfold in eternal reward. To the Church, my heir, [I give] the estate of Dolus, which I built up by my work and which came to me from all sides by my ingenuity: after the day of my death, whatever I shall have worked there, with houses, slaves, vineyards, fields, meadows, cultivated and uncultivated [land], and all its right and boundary, which I drew there by just order, I assign you, holy Church, to have it entire.

To the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul [I give] the estates which I bought for a price paid, that is Gaviacum, Colonica, Landolenas, and Ferrenis, acquired from all sides by my efforts, and whatever there was at Cellis or at Samarciagum near the city of Le Mans, whatever there was at Portithorengum, which I received in guardianship, and what Ceta and Mancia and Guntha were seen to have possessed there by right, and which came into my control, both lands, vineyards, and *coloni* (tenant farmers) and serfs, in their entire portion. Likewise the estates which I bought in honour of the basilica of the lords Peter and Paul with the money which the glorious lord King Chlothar gave us, or which we gained from all sides for our loyalty. These are the estates: Campocunanae, Ludina, and Comariagum, and Cambariacum, as the bills of sale show; I wish that basilica to possess them in God's name, as we have already handed them over there, with the hamlet named Piciniacum, which Gondobaldus, the late deacon, held, and likewise Iliacum, which we received from the illustrious man Babiso. I also establish and decree this: that whatever has been given to me in small items or in any manner whatever, or is known to be written in my charters, which may perhaps have slipped my memory in this sheet of my will, all this entire, you, holy Church, and the venerable basilica of the lords Peter and Paul, are to divide in equal share to possess. As for the estate of Morenacum, which I acquired by my effort and with great labour, and which afterwards, while I was absent by force for the keeping of my loyalty, was seized by Modeghiselus by wrongful means, and, when God gave justice to the lord King Chlothar, came again into the ownership of the holy Church and mine: I establish that you, holy Church, have that estate with all its right and boundary. To the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul [I give] the portion which I am seen to possess there, with the *colonica* which Leodaldus conferred on me by deed of gift, with what I afterwards bought there from all sides, in that holdings of Mechense and Voligio, with all entirety, their portions and boundaries, and slaves, movables and immovables: may you, holy basilica, own [them] perpetually. Yet it is unknown to no one how, after the passing of the late King Guntram, I gave an indissoluble oath to my lord King Chlothar, because the city of Le Mans, by lawful order, after the passing of lord Guntram, ought to have come to him from the inheritance of his father of good memory, the late King Chilperic; but through greed that city was taken from him, and he suffered much loss of the rest of his kingdom; but since my oath bound me entirely, so that I should in no way abandon him, it was easier for me to leave behind, as far as my means went, both the holy Church and my property, than to be found a perjurer (which God forbid). But since out of love for that prince I stood with him with one mind, [because of] his earlier despoiling and the later one, which he endured unjustly, it was necessary for that prince to add something for us, by which we and our poor might sustain the substance of life; for which may that heavenly King be the rewarder on our behalf. For we poor men have neither gold nor silver with which to repay you, most glorious lord Chlothar, with good things; yet from what your glory has conferred on us, we shall presume to remember your highness in this our will. We therefore offer to your royal power from your own gifts, concerning which you granted us, by a precept confirmed by the strength of your hand, licence to do what we wished, that is the estates of Neolone and Walionnum, with all the boundary and appurtenances belonging to them, and whatever was improved for us afterwards: may your highness receive this into its ownership. Likewise we give to you, most glorious lady Queen Berchirudis, the estate named Penpinas, which is called Cella, which our glorious lord, your husband, conferred on us as his gift, so that you may receive that estate, with houses, slaves, and its boundary, after my death, into your control without any hindrance. Let my sweetest nephew Sigechelmus and my great-nephew Toringus, if they survive me, divide in equal share the estate of Seuvacum [and] the hamlet of Ripariola.

Likewise the estate of Briomilia, which was justly owed to us by succession from our kinsmen, and was taken from us for a long time during the interregna, and afterwards, when God gave lord Chlothar his kingdom entire, his piety restored that estate to us and confirmed it by his precept: this estate I wish to be given to my sweetest great-nephews, sons of Sigechelmus, Leutrannus and Sichrannus. Likewise the estate of Castalio, situated in the Saintonge, which belonged to my kinsmen and to the illustrious man Sigelenus, and which the glorious lord King Chlothar granted us by his precept, because it had now for a long time been taken from me and from my aforesaid kinsman Sigelenus: if that Sigelenus survives me, let him recall it into his control; but if not, I wish it to be given to his sons, that is Sichelecus and Berchelaicus. The estates of Crisciagum and Botilo, which are justly owed to us by succession from our father, and which I would have had to share with my brothers if death had not taken them first: now I order that you, my sweetest nephew Sigechelmus, together with my nephew Thoringus, divide those small estates in equal share. The estate of Bualo, situated in the district of Étampes beside Aequalina, which I gave by deed of gift to my sweetest great-nephew Leuthrannus on his wedding day, as that gift contains: by this my will too I wish it to be given to them. The small place called Fontanidum, which the glorious lord King Chlothar granted me as his gift, where Eusebius, the late layman, planted vineyards and where we afterwards also placed slaves: let the holy basilica of the lords Peter and Paul recall into its ownership that small place with all the entirety that is seen to belong there, wholly and entire, and let my great-nephew Leuthramnus and his wife possess half of the vineyards perpetually.

To the basilica of my lord and special godfather Bishop Germanus, who most sweetly brought me up and by his holy prayer brought me, unworthy as I was, to the honour of the episcopate: if it remains so that [he lies] in the basilica of lord Vincent, where his holy little body rests, I give there, in honour of his burial, the estate of Bobane, which is in the district of Étampes on the river Calla, which the most glorious lord King Chlothar conferred on me as his gift; so that if his body is to be moved into the new basilica which the renowned late King Chilperic built, if it should be agreed that it be transferred there, that estate shall always serve wherever his body is, and may the holy bishop himself deign to pray for my misdeeds. I ask the abbot of that illustrious place that my name be recited in the book of life.

My hamlet, which is in the district of Cramtenum at Summa Vedantia, as it is possessed by me at the present time and came lawfully to me by succession from my lord and father, I wish to be given after my death to the basilica of the lords Peter and Paul for the reward of my soul. To my sweetest great-nephew Thoringus I give the *colonica* called Villa Nova, which I bought for a price paid from the son of the late Papolenus; let him hold and possess it in perpetuity. The estate of Idguinum I wish to be given to my sweetest nephew Segechelmus while he lives. After his death I direct that his sons, who are known to have been born of Bertichildis, daughter of Leutramnus, are to possess it, without sharing with their brothers, if he has other sons. The little vineyards and meadows which are at Riulio, and adjoin the vineyards of the holy Church or [lie] within the boundary of Calimarcense, which I bought for a price paid, I wish to be given to the holy Church. Likewise the *colonica* of Satovera, which the late Vulfarius held, and which Aiga afterwards gave us together with the bills of sale she had received from that Vulfarius: that small place with its vineyards and with all its right you, holy Church my heir, are to receive; and the small place called Condomas, which I received in exchange for property of mine and afterwards granted by deed of gift to my most faithful Cottana: I wish that the aforesaid Cotta and her sons may possess that small place entire in perpetuity. As for the house within the walls of the city of Paris, which was built and possessed by the late Eusebius and is known to have been granted to me by the most exalted lord King Chlothar, I decree that it be possessed equally between the holy Church of Le Mans and the holy basilica, my heirs; in such a way that from the shops which are known to be within the house, the rent which is expected from there each year be applied to lighting in the most holy Church of Le Mans and the aforesaid basilica of the lords Peter and Paul; and the plots which are outside the city they are likewise to possess in common.

We have established this to be observed: that whatever [is found] on the day of my death in the house named above in Paris, whether in one [thing] or in any goods whatever which are known to be our own, my heirs, the holy Church of Le Mans and the basilica of the lords Peter and Paul, shall divide equally between themselves. It had almost been consigned by me to oblivion, but by the inspiration of divine grace I remembered [it]. The little vineyards beside the arena, insofar as I recovered them, very largely from waste land, and brought them together, from the arena itself as far as the road, as the enclosure itself surrounds [them], which the holy basilica of the lords Peter and Paul is seen to possess at the present time; and likewise the little vineyards, small meadows and land which are on the right side of the road which goes to Pontlieue, which I bought from my venerable brother Abbot Eoladus, which is known to be in the town of that basilica; with the *brogilum* (enclosed wood) which I redeemed from my brother Abbot Leusius, forty *solidi* having been given, and the small fields which we exchanged with that abbot, which are by the bed of the Sarthe, with the meadow which is at the confluence: let [the basilica] own all of it, wholly and entire, with the servants whom I have placed there, or may yet, Christ being favourable, be able to place there, as it is now possessed by that holy basilica in the name of God, in perpetuity. In the same way, half of the *colonica* of Vatilonnum, which I bought from Bero in the name of that holy basilica, and the other half, which the illustrious matron Egydia conferred on that holy place by deed of gift, I order to remain there entire and in perpetuity, just as from now it is possessed by that basilica under Christ's protection.

And since it is unknown to no one how Berthechisilus, in unlawful manner and against the decrees of the canons, attacked [me] in my see, and caused very grievous loss to the property of holy Mary and to my own property on these grounds; and he did not make restitution as he ought, except in small measure out of my own property, which he had wrongfully alienated: he gave small places with a deed of sale, that is, with houses, [and] he sold us his portion in Bariacum and Vivale entire. And afterwards, when on another occasion the glorious lord Chlothar suffered plots against his kingdom, and I was again in captivity, much on his account, and at that time the not-to-be-named Berthegisilus, ravager of the Church, came again, found in the archive of the Church the deed which he had earlier made, and ordered it to be burnt with fire: so may the fearful and terrible Judge hold judgement with him over his deeds. And after our lord, by the will of God, entered into friendship with his most exalted cousin King Theudebert, and willingly received a portion of his kingdom, we too, despite opposition, recalled those small places into our ownership. Campariacum and Estivale, with houses, slaves, vineyards and woods, meadows, waters and watercourses, and their rights and all livestock, I assign to the holy basilica of the lords Peter and Paul. I have completed, namely, the house within the walls, on the right side of the postern, which I built by my own work, where a small oratory has been constructed in honour of the holy archangel Michael; I wished that those houses should belong to the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul.

While we were detained with lord King Chlothar for our loyalty and our love of him, the Church's bakehouse was built in front of that house; therefore in these places the Church [provides] allowances, and the *matricula* (register of poor), which I set up there: I humbly beg my lord bishop, whoever shall be my successor, that this *matricula* may at all times, just as up to now in these times it has earned its allowances, always henceforward be fed, the holy Church providing, and that the house itself be for the reception of bishops, or of the religious who serve that oratory: for miracles too have been shown there, and it ought to be honoured and venerated in all things. We pray our lord and bishop, our successor, and adjure him by God of the Trinity, that from the estates which I have assigned to the holy Church by this sheet of my will, or which were acquired in my time, or came to the holy Church by gift, from all and in all, the tithes of grain, wine, cheese, bacon, all the tithes, be gathered every year in that house of the holy archangel Michael, as was done in our time, and be distributed to the poor and pilgrims for their sustenance: for the holy Church will not suffer loss thereby; and may what we, though unworthy, who were seen to occupy such a place of the episcopate as it was, strove with God's assent to distribute among the poor, be maintained by you without ceasing. To the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul [I give] that courtyard with the houses which the late priest Romolus, of good memory, held in the city of Le Mans, and that house which he built in our times upon the walls, to which we too lent a hand, and which we afterwards bought from his niece; let the aforesaid church be able to possess those houses perpetually, as they are possessed from the present time in the name of God by that holy basilica, with whatever has been worked there, or was annexed before or in my time, wholly and entire, without hindrance from anyone.

To the holy Church my heir I give the estate called Grandefontana, which I bought for a price paid from Vaddolenus, my co-godfather, son of Bavo, with all its right and its bounds. To you, holy basilica of the lords Peter and Paul, I give the estate of Conadacum, which I bought for a price paid from the matron Belletrudis or Bettana, widow of the late Maurinus, with the estates of Colicas, which I afterwards [bought] for a price paid from Betholenus and Mantharigus, with the woods and all appurtenances belonging to them, with houses and slaves, as I have already handed [them] into your control: I wish [it] to be given entire with movables and immovables, with that small field named Timiagum, which we hold in usufruct from my son and kinsman Berulfus, and after my death you are to recall it into your power. To my sweetest nephew Sigechelmus, although in times past I already conferred by deed of gift the estate of Murocinctum, which was lawfully due [to me] by succession from my lord and father, and afterwards, my sins causing it, my brother Berthulfus was killed on campaign with lord King Chlothar, and his portion lawfully came to me, I have wished it to be included in this my will, so that both what I gave him before and what afterwards came to me from my brother, wholly and entire, my nephew himself, that estate with houses, slaves, vineyards, fields, meadows, woods, waters and watercourses, movables and immovables, as he is already seen to possess it, may own perpetually, both he and his offspring. The third portion of that estate of Murocinctum, which my brother Ermenulfus of good memory held and gave to me, I wish to be given after my death to my sweetest great-nephew, the son of that Sigechelmus, named Leodefredus, except that those whom he freed, or whom I redeemed from captivity, are to remain free. The house which is within the walls of the city of Le Mans, which my lord and brother Bishop Chaimoaldus built while he was performing the office of archdeacon, with the small house which the deacon Malaricus held: I wish that my sweetest nephew Sigechelmus, to whom I gave them, and his sons, own them in perpetuity, since the new house is known to stand on those purchased plots.

The estate of Patriliacum, which is beside Pontochiuggane, which I once bought from Dolenus, and [took] the sale in the name of Saints Peter and Paul and their basilica, which we were already at that time seen to be building, and afterwards assigned to that holy basilica: I wish it to possess it in perpetuity, with the *colonicae* belonging to it. The estate of Monciacum, with the *colonica* which I bought and joined to it, whether founded [there] or from all around in the same districts of Condacum or Monciacum: I wish it to be given entire to you, holy Church my heir. The vineyards which the lord Bishop Licinius of holy memory gave me as his gift out of affection, beside the vineyards of Cariliacum, and [the land] which we had earlier bought with the land from the late Sargitus, a merchant, by divine favour, and afterwards planted vineyards there, and joined them in one enclosure with the vineyards of the holy church: we wish the holy church of Le Mans to possess this for the reward of our soul. Although formerly that field had few vines, and my lords the bishops, my predecessors, would not add anything there, we, for love of the holy Church and its increase, greatly enlarged it, both from merchants and from others, and paid the price; we desire that they may serve the right and ownership of the holy Church. Likewise the little vineyards which are in the Saboranense, which I joined together from all sides by my own work, whether by gift or by purchase, and if I can yet add more, with their cultivators and households, together with the house which stands there, I order you, holy Church of the lords Peter and Paul, to have.

Concerning Pontlieue, this is about the *matricula* (register of poor) and the *synodochium* (hospice) in honour of Saint Martin, which is a dependency of Saint Peter and Paul, at Pontlieue. If we weigh each thing, how great our misdeeds are known to have been, committed while we were held in the world, the means of redeeming them are not as great as the faults committed; but may almighty God, who wills that none should perish, Himself, out of the generous grace of His goodness, grant some pardon for those small little gifts which we are seen to offer with great tears and a mindful soul to our Redeemer in the persons of the poor. Therefore, since it is my vow and my free and considered decision that the basilica which [I built] in honour of our most blessed and special patron Martin, the holy bishop, at Pontlieue, where by God's favour I have also placed his holy relics, I assign, and I order and decree that that holy place have the small estates by these names: Longiagas, Nogent, Novavilla, Antoniacum, and of Monasteriolum that part which I bought from Leodelena for a price paid, and at Avantum whatever I bought there, or from wherever it came to me, with slaves, movables and immovables, and all their rights, and whatever more I may be able to add or buy for those places; and let it remain under the abbot and the authority of the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul. Although it is presumptuous to say that the place is a *synodochium*, since we have brought little there, yet God and that holy athlete of Christ are able to bestow very much there, whereby the poor may be clothed and fed, and all our friends and pilgrims may be seen to have shelter in our memory. For the present we order that sixteen little souls devoted to God, that is, poor men, blind or infirm, be placed in that place; and that food be supplied to them sufficiently every day, by reckoning made. And, as we mentioned above, from the tribute of Taletum, and the aid from Crisciacum and Cambariacum, as we have already ordered above, both in clothing and in bedding and in footwear, [be given] both to these our brothers and to the *matricularii* of Saint Peter who are known to be under its rule; you, abbot of the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul, let it be above all your utmost care to fulfil this for them in every respect. But if in anything (which God forbid) you prove negligent in this, you shall render account before the tribunal of Christ with the holy apostles Peter and Paul, and the holy bishop Martin. And let none of the bishops our successors presume to take away anything that has been assigned to the aforesaid place or to the poor; but at that festival let both the bishop and all the clergy receive a worthy meal; and if anyone withdraws anything else from the aforesaid small estates, let him be judged in the sight of God as a murderer of the poor. And you, venerable abbot, and your successors, take such care of the office of the holy church of lord Martin as of that of Saints Peter and Paul; and let light through the nights be sufficiently provided from the tribute of those estates, and let what remains benefit the poor and needy of that basilica.

The estate of Blacciacum, situated in the territory of Bordeaux beside the fort of Blaye, which is on the bed of the Garonne, although it was possessed for a long time by my parents, was taken from my mother's ownership during the interregna and in her youth; and by Aunulfus son of Maurilio, who had seized it, two parts of that estate were unlawfully bequeathed by the pages of his will to holy churches, namely those of Bordeaux, Tours and Angoulême; the third Arnulfus, the brother of that Aunulfus, possessed. Hence we had disputes between ourselves and them over the aforesaid estate; but he, recognising that it was lawfully owed to us, in the presence of those bishops who were seen to possess two parts of it, returned to us at once a third of everything in that estate, and handed us a letter thereon confirmed by his own hand and signed by the aforesaid bishops, for us to possess. But since divine love so constrains us that we do not proceed against a holy Church, perhaps we may redeem the property with the good will of my lords and brothers. But since lord Agericus, bishop [of Tours], sold us that portion which belonged to Saint Martin, and made the sale to us together with his canons, and we paid at once sixty *solidi*, which it was worth by his own valuation, and added our claim to it, we wish that you, my holy heir, the Church of Le Mans, possess it; and if we can still redeem anything in that property from the houses of the bishops of Bordeaux or Angoulême, recall it wholly and entire into your power.

The *colonica* of Vincentiana, which my lady mother possessed, and which we now in God's name are seen to possess, which is beside that field of Blaviacum, I wish to be given to the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul with slaves, vineyards and lands. The estate of Floriacum, situated between the two seas, which belonged to my parents and afterwards my mother lost through being orphaned, and which was wrongfully possessed by Childegernus, half of which estate, with slaves, houses, vineyards, woods and all its bounds and appurtenances, I redeemed for a price paid from Bertram, or Betto, the son of that Childegernus: I wish that that estate, which belonged to my parents, be owned in perpetuity by the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul. The house within the walls of the city of Bordeaux, which I and my brother Ermenulfus recovered by our own effort, that stone-built house with its appurtenances, we order to pass into the ownership of our sweetest nephew Sigechelmus, that he may have and possess it and leave it to his descendants to possess. And we order this: that for all the time of their lives, whenever envoys of the lords and venerable [clergy] of the holy Church of Le Mans or of the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul come there to trade for fish, they always have lodging in that house, and buy there what they need. The place called Bresetum in the territory of Bordeaux, where we are seen to have *precarii* [another reading: pitch-workers], and which we bought for a price paid from the late Arennoaldus: that property, with the *precarii* living there and their households, and the pitch-works, as it is possessed by me at present, after my death you, holy and venerable basilica of the lord Peter and Paul, recall into your ownership, so that pitch may be received from it every year.

It is known to all how twice or three times I suffered despoiling in the property of the holy Church and in my own. God knows that I did not suffer this for our faults, but because I wished to keep faith unbroken; and the holy Church at that time suffered grave loss in its holdings; and I, a poor man, escaped greatly impoverished in my own small substance. Therefore I blush to write how little has remained to offer. I give that silver which God, the lord king, or friends afterwards bestowed on us, as the list written in my hand states, for I have arranged that two parts of that silver which I am seen to have acquired, you, most holy Church, shall receive; the other portion, which I wrote down in that list, I order you, basilica of Saint Peter and Paul, whom I have instituted my heir as I did you, holy Church, to have. I adjure by the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, both you, lord bishop, who will succeed, and you, abbot, who will be in office at the time when God commands me to depart from this world, and your successors, that none presume to take away anything of these items or sell any of those small little gifts which I [gave] to the holy Church and the holy basilica in commemoration of my name, but that they must endure perpetually at all times, both for the adornment of the holy Church and basilica and for their altars. As for the remaining bit of silver, whatever is found in my little storeroom after the day of my death, and which I have not assigned, saving the silver of the holy Church excepted, I order that what I am seen to have at present, or may yet acquire, that has not been assigned, be divided wholly and equally between the holy Church and the holy basilica of the lord Peter and Paul; and if it is necessary to adorn my tomb somewhat, and I have not done this beforehand, let the abbot, from the portion he received, and from what he received correspondingly from the bishop, deign to [provide] for my tomb and take care to arrange it from that; and if Christ permits us to remain in this light, let that silver be put to making vessels for the service of the basilica, where needed.

Likewise I order concerning the *damea* [another reading: *clavia*] garments: you, sweetest archdeacon, whoever you are at that time, I order to offer reverently to the lord bishop, my successor, two of the best pieces from my own *damea* garments. And to you, holy archdeacon, I instruct that you take one good horse and one small pair from my property. Everything that is found in my little storeroom after my death, whether from my property or from my service, or the goods or garments which I earned or acquired, except what is the property of the holy Church, I order to be made into three portions: one let my lord and successor the bishop receive; the second the basilica of the lord Peter and Paul; the third I order to be distributed at once to the poor. Likewise I instruct you, archdeacon, and call God to witness, that of the produce which I leave in that year when I have closed my last day, a third part be distributed by your hand to the poor without fraud.

Likewise I wish and order that all the servants of the holy Church who are known to be officials, and my own, both clerics and laymen, who are seen to live with me, receive at once one horse each, whether freeborn, freedmen or servants; and the remaining horses, both stallions and geldings and foals, which are found and bore the brand of the holy Church, let the bishop and the Church receive them all. Those which bore my own personal brand, or which kinsmen or friends gave me, let the holy Church receive half of them; and let the basilica, or the abbot who is there, collect the other half. I wished this to be added to this will: that of the herds of horses which my littleness gathered from all sides or increased, except the old mares, two portions be made, as we have said, of those herds which are seen to be my own and have pasture on the land of the holy Church: let the holy Church receive one, and let the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul receive the other. That herd which is seen to keep the horse-portions on the property of the holy basilica of the lord bishop Victurius, I wish to be given to that holy basilica. The mares of that man which were the personal property of Gallimere I wish to be given to my faithful Elopodia.

The estate of Marciliacum, situated beside the village of Jublains, which I bought for a price paid from Medighiselus and Ebretrudis, or added to from all sides, or may still add to, with houses and slaves and its appurtenances, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, I give and transfer in perpetual ownership to my sweetest great-nephew Leodochrannus. Likewise the estate beside the village of Pacilenus, which the father Blado Victribernus [another reading: Bladovicus, tribune?] of the *bessi* sold us for our *solidi*: that property with all its appurtenances I order my sweetest great-nephew Sigramnus to have. Likewise the estate of Pauliacum, which I bought for a price paid, that is three hundred *solidi* in gold, from the venerable Bobenus, abbot of the basilica of the lord Albinus, I order my sweetest great-nephew Leodochrannus to have, that he may possess it in perpetuity. So also, if either the basilica of the lord Albinus, or the abbot who is the successor of that Bobenus, makes any attempt concerning these [lands], let him make double restitution to the said Leudochrannus, and even so he shall not be able to claim the estate, if he wishes to act against the settlement of his predecessor; and so let it be held by my great-nephew in perpetuity. The estate which is known to be beside the village of Berulfus, and in that estate Berulfus, who formerly lost [it], whatever I bought there, both from the son of Enulfus and from Remoaldus and his wife, I wish to be given wholly and entire to my sweetest great-nephews Leutfredus and Thoringus, if they survive me, to be divided equally between them; so also that after my death they recall it wholly into their power.

To the basilica of the holy and most blessed Saint Germanus, bishop of Paris, who tenderly brought me up, and through whose intercession I came to the burden of the priesthood, though I did not deserve it: I built that basilica in his honour by the city of Le Mans [another reading: before the city], and built houses there, and established monks, who, Christ being favourable, may there perform the office and service for all time. I give to that basilica in honour of that bishop these estates with these men: Charisagum, with the vineyards which are at the village of Silviacum, and the small property called Stirpiacum, with the small vineyards and the few slaves known to be there, Landolenae, Graciacum and Manciacum, which I bought for a price from all sides and which came into my ownership, both what I am seen to possess at present and what I may yet improve: I wish them to be given to that holy basilica in honour of the most blessed lord Germanus; and those vineyards which are at Ruilio, which Aunigiselus the deacon held, or which I afterwards bought from all sides, with half the meadow at that Ruilio, I instruct that holy basilica to possess. The estate of Comancium, which I bought from my son and kinsman Ebroaldus, and afterwards built houses and vineyards there, with what I found [there], with all its rights and appurtenances, I decree that you, basilica of Saint Peter and Paul, which I built in your honour and appointed as my immediate heir in all things, are to have. The small property called Fontanae, within the bounds of Alençon, which the magnificent man Baudhegiselus and his wife Saucia granted me and made deeds of gift for, and we gave them much help where we could: that property, after our death, you, holy Church and venerable basilica of the lord Peter and Paul, recall into your ownership, as it was possessed by that Baudeghiselus; so also that their names be recited in the book of life in that basilica. The estate of Redonatiacum, which always belonged to Bonalfa, and there afterwards we [added] both lands and woods which we bought for a price from Chargarius and Ragnaricus, or from all sides, wholly and entire, as that estate of Redonatiacum always belonged to Bonalfa and ought to belong there, that it may profit the holy Church, my heir, in perpetuity.

Although we wished that whatever had been acquired by us, both in lands and in movables and immovables, as our earlier will contained, I have already assigned all of it wholly and entire in one will: yet since afterwards, after God ordered the whole kingdom of the Franks to come under the rule of our glorious lord King Chlothar, and afterwards his generous kindness regarded us in some measure for our services, it is not fitting for us to pass that over either. Therefore those estates which Avitus of blessed memory, son of the late bishop Felix, who had married our kinswoman and near relative, [held], and all the property of Avitus, which his kindness granted between me and the illustrious man Gundoland, mayor of the palace, and which I am now seen to hold at present jointly with him: my whole portion, both what is in the Berry and in the Albigeois, Quercy and the Agenais, wholly and entire, whatever half of that land belongs to my share, for the remission of my sins in whatever measure, you, basilica of Saint Peter and Paul, whom I appointed heir, after my death receive those estates in their entirety; and the estate of Nogiogilum, which I and the illustrious man Gundoland granted in usufruct to my daughter and kinswoman Dundana, after her death you, most holy Church and basilica, recall jointly into your power by halves, as was agreed in the *precaria* of the said matron, dividing it equally.

The estate of Vocriomnum, which the glorious lord King Chlothar [gave] me as his gift for our property which Egulfus and Arnoaldus wrongfully both held and laid waste, although the pious king had already given us more for it, but at his injunction I released this to the Church of Metz in honour of the lord Stephen, and I sought this estate with my lord and brother Bishop Arnulf, so that he received those estates which had been Egulfus' and Arnoaldus'; we were to hold the estate of Vocriomnum in perpetuity, and have free choice of what we wished to do with it. Therefore that estate, both for the reward of the lord king and for our own, since the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul has few vineyards, hence in this place, that estate with all its rights and the appurtenances belonging to it, wholly and entire, I wish to be given in perpetuity to you, holy basilica of the lord Peter and Paul, where I desire my poor body to be buried. The estate of Nociogilum, which is in the territory of Poitiers on the bed of the Loire, which Beatus, nephew of the late Babo, son of Theudaldus, granted there from his maternal inheritance by title of donation, I order you, most holy basilica of the lord Peter and Paul, to have after my death.

From Marogilum, the estates of Rufiniacum and Marogilum, which came to me from the holdings of Nunciana, who greatly laid waste the property of the holy Church, and which our glorious lord King Chlothar granted to us after the death of that Nunciana, I order you, most holy Church, my heir, to have. The small estate called Lucianus, whatever Hisigilus owes there; that small property on the river Loir, called Bauciallum, which I bought from Bestingiselus of the Vendômois and his wife and stepsons, I wish to be given to the basilica of Saint Victurius in the city of Le Mans, with the slaves and all that has been improved there. The estate called Tauriacum: that portion which Nuncia held there, and which we now hold by precept of our lord, as we hold Marogilum and Rufiniacum; and that estate of Tauriacum, both the portion which was Nunciana's and has now come into our possession, and also that portion which Audericus and his nephews, the son of his brother and of his sister, sold to us, and which we joined together, I order you, most holy Church, my heir, to have. The small estate called Luciacus, whatever I bought there from Berthigisillus, or his wife and their sons, and am seen to possess at present, with whatever I have added there or may yet be able to add, I assign to the basilica of Saint Peter and Paul, my heir, to possess. The estates situated in the territory of Châteaudun, that is, the estate of Pannonium, which I bought from Abbot John for a price, namely one hundred and forty *solidi*, and the estate of Marciriae, which I am likewise seen to have bought from Betho, son of the late Baddo: those small properties you, my dearest nephew Sigechelmus, are to receive after my death; so also that after your death your sons divide them equally among themselves.

Those small properties which Suadria, sister of the late Bishop Theoderus, gave to the holy Church by her testament, that is, Luciniacum and Mons, and which I afterwards reclaimed by my own effort. The estate on the Loire which I bought from Dudo, nephew of Romonus, that is, for one hundred *solidi*: that property, whatever I am seen to hold there at present, with houses, vineyards, lands, slaves and that whole portion, I order you, most holy Church, my heir, to have. Likewise the estate of Brea, which Theudoaldus sold me: recall that too into your ownership, with vineyards, slaves and all its rights. The estate of Kairacum, which I bought from the deacon Comerius for three hundred *solidi*, and which is now known to be in my ownership in God's name, I decree that you, holy basilica of the lord Peter and Paul, whom I named heir together with the church, are to have, with houses, slaves, vineyards, meadows, woods, with all its rights; and if I can yet improve anything there, recall it wholly and entire into your power. The estate of Sitriacum, which I bought for a price from Leugadius, with another small estate called Blaciacus, with the appurtenances belonging to them, houses, slaves, vineyards, lands, meadows, woods, and all their rights, I direct you, most holy Church of Le Mans, my heir, to have.

The estates of Cresciacum and Vallis, as was agreed by letters between me and the lord Arnulf, bishop of the Church of Metz, in honour of the lord Stephen of his Church, as I already decreed earlier by our letter: after my death let that holy Church in honour of Saint Stephen recall them into its ownership, and let whoever is bishop at that time order my name to be written there in the book of life. Three parts of a *colonica*, which we had from the holdings of Arngaldus, I order the basilica of the lord Peter and of our special patron Bishop Medard to have after my death. The estate of Montiniacum, which the late Bishop Giboaldus held, and which afterwards came into our ownership, I now assign and decree to be the holy Church's by right, with all its rights. The estates situated in Burgundy, which our glorious lord King Chlothar gave to us and to the illustrious men Brado and Warnacharius, mayor of the palace, which had belonged to the late Leudegiselus: the third portion which is due to me from those estates by lawful order together with those illustrious men, I wish you, most holy Church of Le Mans and basilica of Saint Peter and Paul, my heirs, to have equally with them. And the estates in Provence, which that pious king gave between me and the illustrious men Gondolaidus and Chugus from the holdings of Aureliana: as much of them as we could rightfully claim by justice without sin on our part, that is, my portion of those estates, you, my heirs, recall into your power together with those illustrious men. The estate from the holdings of Nunciana, both in Poitou and in Erbaticola, and also those other estates which [I hold] with Chiso, my fellow godfather, in Quercy, the Limousin, or wherever in Gothia the portion of Nunciana was lawfully rendered to us from it: I direct you, my dearest fellow godfather Chiso, for the affection of love and of our godparenthood, to have [them], to divide equally with your and our nephew Thoringus. The estates which I bought for a price from Dracoaldus, bishop [of Auch], and which are known to lie in that city where the said bishop was killed, I direct you, my dearest nephew Sigechelmus, to possess together with your sons. My most faithful Warnacharius and Walco, son of the late Tedemondus, who are known to have served me faithfully from their youth and the holy Church with complete loyalty, as is unknown to no one: whatever I gave them in lands, slaves, vineyards, or they are seen to have acquired in my time, I wish to be granted to them wholly and entire, and let their sons and daughters possess it as long as they live, and I order and decree that none take anything from them.

Whatever we gave to our late faithful man Cherulfus or to his sons, we confirm this entire. To my most faithful friend Chadelenus, whatever I gave him here and in the territory of Le Mans, I wish that he and his sons possess it in perpetuity, since it is known to all that he served faithfully and constantly in the offices of the holy church, and intends to do so in his lifetime, and it is just that whatever [was given] him from the Church's right, or what came to the Church by my labour, should always remain with him perpetually. To my faithful man Betolenus, son of the late Cundelenus, whatever they gave his father, or what was afterwards granted to that Betolenus by our generosity, I wish to be given in perpetuity to that Betolenus and his wife, and to their sons: so also that his mother possess in usufruct whatever she has of it as long as she lives. After her death let the said Betolenus and his sons receive it entire, and let them always remain friends of the Church.

This, therefore, I ask and order: that however many my friends or faithful servants may be, my upbringing of them and the kindness I spent on them may always be remembered by them, so that they too, after my death, take care always to be present there when the day of my commemoration comes, and give support to the abbot of that place, and say: 'Happy is that man who leaves good friends behind.' I direct you, my dearest nephew Sigechelmus, and I ask and adjure your sons by almighty God, that as long as He wills you to survive in the world, together with your wives and offspring, if health permits, you always visit my little tomb two or three times each year; and this I adjure the abbot of that place, that he refresh you fully and honour your sons, in the way the holy Church knows I was its comforter, so that it may please you and your sons to visit that holy place often and to commemorate my memory. I adjure and ask my lord Bishop Chaimoaldus, since he is known to be my kinsman, and since divine kindness has brought him to the summit of the priesthood, that he always remember my upbringing of him and the patronage of Saint Peter, from which he went forth, Christ presiding, to that burden: that with fitting burial, whenever God bids me depart from this light, they with their own hands, with his other lords and brothers, graciously bury my poor body, so that thereby they may gain the Lord's reward and praise may spread among the people. This I order the archdeacon of that time: that to those lords who deign to bury a sinner they give two pairs of horses, and gather two colts, and let those lords each receive a pair; and you, lord Chaimoaldus, graciously do this with the archdeacon, and we order that you receive in like manner as your brothers receive. And as long as God wills you to survive in the world, I ask that you deign to come to my commemoration; and let the lord abbot and the congregation of Saint Peter and Paul show you fitting honour.

These men and these women I order to be free: Libigiselus with his wife and sons, Chinemundus, Chrodosindus with his wife and children, Theodogundis and her son Lopus, and her daughter, Emma with his wife and sons, Ebrelenus with his wife and sons, Gariulfus, Julianus, Picoaldus with his wife and sons, [and] the son and daughter of Maurellus. Likewise also my servants who are seen to serve there, both of Roman and of barbarian birth. These are: Teodanes, Bajo, Baudasindus, Maurus, Austreharius, Audisgisilus, Vetesigilus, Bercehanus, Quotanes, Alagisus, Leodegiselus, and the sons of Theodonivia. All these I order to be freeborn wholly, with all their personal property which they have or may be able to earn hereafter, and may they deserve to have the protection of the holy basilica of the lord Apostles Peter and Paul, where in God's name I desire my poor body to rest; so that each of them gather at the time of my burial [anniversary], and offer the oblations, solely in my name, before the holy altar, and recite [it], and each in God's name observe on the said day the service such as they are seen to have performed; and let them give help to the abbot of that place, and afterwards, on the next day, let the abbot give them a most worthy meal, and let each return to their homes: both those whose names are contained here, and those of barbarian race whom I bought afterwards or may yet be able to buy, both boys and girls, who are known to have been bought by me and to whom I have made letters [of freedom]; and let them remain in complete freedom, and observe this, as many of them [as there are], and let all continue under the guardianship and protection of Saint Peter; and those of them who wish to stay with the abbot or to serve the basilica, let them be enriched from the property of the holy basilica, so that it may better please them to pay honour to my poor tomb and to serve the holy basilica. And those who are known to live here in the territory of Le Mans are recognised to have the protection of the holy basilica of the lord Apostles Peter and Paul. If it be necessary, let that abbot also, to whom the holy basilica has been committed to rule and govern, at all times, from what I have conferred there, take care to celebrate my burial [anniversary] and the light of my poor tomb every year in such a way as it pleases [others] to enrich other places of the saints with very great property. But if that abbot be negligent in this, let him know that before the tribunal of Christ, with the lords Apostles Peter and Paul, he will have vengeance for it and receive perpetual damnation. As for those from the Church's holdings whom I have released, or shall release, by letters at each festival in white [garments], as their letters show, let them remain under the guardianship and protection of the holy Church.

And because the chances of human life make many things uncertain, and I fear lest (God forbid) wicked greed, which is the root of evils, should in any way break my pious intention, I adjure you, lord bishop, whom God shall will to come after me, by that dread judgement and day, so may you gain the eternal reward of blessedness and not acquire a share of damnation with Judas, that you fulfil the decision of my will in all things, and as long as God wills you to survive, take care to guard everything. This freedom he ought to weigh who firmly desires the judgement of his own will to endure. I ask that, when my testament has been opened before all and before my fellow-provincials, then by the hand of the archdeacon one hundred *solidi* be sent, through the lord bishop of the city of Tours, to the tomb of the lord and my particular patron, Saint Martin the bishop, where I laid down my hair [at tonsure] and have paid my tribute there each year. Likewise let fifty *solidi* be directed to the basilica of Saint Albinus the bishop by the hand of the bishop of Angers; these *solidi*, in separate bags with sealed little notes for each place, as I mentioned above, I have entrusted into the hand of a faithful steward, to be distributed as the page of my testament declares.

To you, archdeacon, I commission and direct that through all the basilicas which are known to be around our city [you distribute as follows]: that is, to the basilica of Saint Victurius, my particular patron, you shall give 20 *solidi*. To the basilica of the lord Vincent, where Saint Domnolus the bishop rests, in honour of that martyr and of the lord bishop, you shall give 20 *solidi*. To the basilica of Saint Mary and the Holy Cross you shall give 10 *solidi*. To the basilica of Saint Julian the bishop you shall give either a horse or 5 *solidi* in gold; likewise to the basilica of Saint Richomer [...] *solidi*. To the basilica of Saint Hilary you shall give 5 *solidi*. To the oratories of the lord Martin, the lord Victorius, and Saint Peter within the walls you shall give 5 *solidi* in gold or in horses. To the basilica of Saint Stephen the martyr you shall give 5 *solidi* either in gold or in horses. Likewise I wish and order that to all our clergy who are known to serve here in the church you give fifty *solidi*, from whatever [funds] or in whatever goods. This I especially ask: that in the places written above, where I have assigned something, not as was fitting but as far as my means allowed, their priests order my name to be written in the book of life and recited at each festival.

I ought, indeed, to have made known above who should serve my ashes; but because I had not fully examined among my household to whom I should commit this task, therefore it suits me, out of however many estates I have assigned to the holy basilica of the lord Peter and Paul, my heir, to possess, [to choose] one householder from each estate, those who are known to be the more worthy and serve us and the holy basilica faithfully; we wish to write their names in one letter and confirm it with our hand, so that they be released wholly from servitude, and that, together with the abbot, they have full care of my poor tomb, both of the lighting and of my ashes, until the last day of their lives; both they and the offspring who shall be begotten of them ought in perpetuity to serve with complete diligence, and the freedom of their status ought to endure perpetually under the protection of that abbot.

But because we do not presume to assign or release anyone from the household of the holy Church, either for our ashes or for making any disposition, as our lords and predecessors did [not]; in like manner I order that if any of my servants, or of those of my late brother Bertulf, have not come to my mind, and these are seen to live in the territory of Le Mans, they be wholly freed from servitude and deserve to have the protection and guardianship of the holy basilica of the lord Peter and Paul, like my other freedmen. Those whom I redeemed from captivity, who were freeborn before and now are seen to serve for the price, both men and women of the estate of Boalcha, let them all be released from servitude. To the chief *matricula* (register of poor) in the city, and to those that are at the small basilicas, I order five *solidi* to be given by the hand of the archdeacon.

Since I desire the decision of my deliberation to be firmly kept through this testament, therefore I adjure you, lords and bishops, by the holy apostolate which you received by divine tradition, that wherever necessary you always give help to my basilica and to the abbot of that place, and instruct the lord, my successor, with such counsel that he diminish nothing of what I have assigned to the holy basilica in honour of the lord Apostles Peter and Paul for the remedy of my soul, nor defraud it of anything on any pretext, since I know that I have caused no loss to the holy church. Likewise I adjure all of you, by the victories of the most clement princes, who have power of acting in the world with our lords and princes, that if it be necessary you never deny the aid of your protection to this little page. Further I have recalled small matters which I had quite forgotten. The house at Jublains which [I] built by my own work, with the courtyard and stable, and the garden and *colonicas*, whatever I bought on every side, both from Boso the priest and from the heirs of Etolenus [and] Trilonus, at the place called Calviacum, or anywhere in the town of Jublains beside the bank of the little river Aron, both lands, slaves, woods, meadows and all [appurtenances] by their right, with Taxonaria which I claimed successfully against Leuttherus and his heirs, all of it wholly I wish you, holy Church my heir, to have, except the ancient properties of the holy Church of Jublains. Likewise also those portions which Guntherus conferred on me in all his property by deeds of gift, and the adjoining [property] at that house of Jublains, I decree that you, holy mother and my heir the Church, have. Those small houses which the deacon Domnigisilus of good memory held by our gift, and which the poor man built there, and which after his death we granted to our dearest nephew Leodochrannus, with all the small houses, little enclosures, little vineyards, little fields, and whatever the deacon himself was seen to have there, with those few slaves who are seen to be there: we wish that our nephew, as long as for love of us he resolves to come often to the basilica of the Apostles Saint Peter and Paul, as we also wrote in [our] testament, we wish that he always possess them with the favour of the bishop our successor, so also that after his death they return to the right of the holy Church.

For I also declare at present that if anyone should attempt to go against this my will, he shall be struck with perpetual excommunication, and may God show such judgement upon him that, struck with the leprosy of Naaman, the earth may swallow him up like Dathan and Abiram; and may divine vengeance so appear upon him that in the present age he may know he has done wrong, and in the judgement to come may never obtain the pardon of remission. If any smudges, if any erasures, if any letters have been added or removed, I did [it] and ordered [it] to be done, while I read over my will to myself more than once; and I acknowledge and correct everything point by point. As the law teaches, I have entrusted [it] to be secured with the subscriptions and seals of seven honourable men, and I have ordered [them] to be attached for the firmness and stipulation of the whole matter. Done at Le Mans in the city, on the day and in the year stated above. I, Bertram, in the name of Christ, though unworthy, bishop, have read over and subscribed my testament, which I dictated to my son Ebbo the notary to write. I, Guntinus, *honoratus*, subscribed at the request of the lord Bertram. I, Dado, subscribed at the request of the lord Bertram. The mark of Gerinus: I subscribed at the request of the lord Bertram. I, Ibbolenus, subscribed at the request of the lord Bertram. I, Gaddo, subscribed at the request of the lord Bertram. I, Hugo, *honoratus*, subscribed. I, Ebbo the notary, at the command of my lord Bishop Bertram, and in his presence, wrote, read over and subscribed this testament, and noted the day. Likewise I, Bishop Bertram, ask my son the archdeacon that, when my testament has been opened, he himself pursuing [the matter], he have it entered in the municipal records according to the law, so that it may always endure firmly.
